formed.instruction: Read src/app/page.tsx to assess current data-anvil attribute coverage: check for data-anvil-action="primary", data-anvil-action="input", data-anvil-state JSON snapshot, and any restart affordances (data-anvil-action="restart"). Note which elements need wiring or re-wiring for the contract-wiring phase.

Edit src/app/page.tsx to ensure the following data-anvil attributes are present on the route-bound interactive UI: (1) data-anvil-action="primary" on the main submit/create button (e.g. the button that creates a project or adds a task). (2) data-anvil-action="input" on the main text entry surface (e.g. the task title or project name input). (3) data-anvil-state on the main container or status region containing a JSON.stringify snapshot of meaningful visible state that includes at least one dimension immediately responding to user input (e.g. current filter selection, edited title value, or task status count). (4) data-anvil-action="restart" on every restart affordance including terminal and active states (e.g. a reset/reload button or a hook-triggered restart). Preserve existing Next.js app router structure, imports from src/lib/types.ts, and API call patterns. The data-anvil-state JSON must be computed after each render and reflect the current selection or edited value.

Create smoke-check.js at the workspace root. The file must read src/app/page.tsx as a string and assert: (a) the string contains the literal data-anvil-action="primary" (check for the attribute with proper quoting), (b) it contains data-anvil-action="input", (c) it contains data-anvil-state, (d) it contains JSON.stringify or a JSON template literal referencing state, (e) it contains data-anvil-action="restart". Print 'all anvil checks pass' on success or throw an Error listing missing checks. Use fs.readFileSync with utf8 encoding. Do not use shell quoting; write plain JavaScript.

For the nextjs profile, create a runnable Next.js app, not only package metadata. Keep the project in the workspace root unless a project subdirectory already exists. Preserve the language and styling toolchains declared by an existing project. A JavaScript project using plain CSS requires package.json, an App Router page and layout, and the imported stylesheet; do not add TypeScript, @types, Tailwind, PostCSS, or Autoprefixer only to satisfy a template. A TypeScript project additionally requires a coherent tsconfig and type dependencies. If those mode-appropriate files are absent, write the coherent App Router scaffold before further inspection. package.json must include compatible next, react, and react-dom dependencies plus scripts.build = `next build`. If Tailwind is used, package.json must include tailwindcss/postcss/autoprefixer and postcss.config plugins must include BOTH tailwindcss and autoprefixer. For TypeScript/TSX apps, create tsconfig.json before treating the app as complete. Keep a single route-bound implementation; do not leave capability components unimported. Do not use deprecated moduleResolution=node10 or target=ES5; prefer moduleResolution=bundler and target=ES2017 or newer. For interactive UI, expose task-agnostic observability hooks: data-anvil-action="primary" on the main start/submit/action control, data-anvil-action="input" on the main text entry surface when one exists, and data-anvil-state containing JSON for meaningful visible state after each render. The data-anvil-state snapshot must include at least one dimension that immediately responds to input, such as the current selection or edited value. When the contract includes start_or_restart_flow, every restart affordance (including terminal and active states when present) should carry data-anvil-action="restart"; the initial primary action alone cannot satisfy recovery verification. A restart reachable during active use (hook or keyboard shortcut) allows behavioral verification, while an overlay-only restart may verify as unverified:terminal_state_not_reached (partial). The dev/start scripts must run on the explicitly requested port 60302: `next dev -p 60302` and `next start -p 60302` or equivalent `--port 60302` forms.
